body.description: Demonstrates the two-run HITL approval pattern. Run 1 drafts an outbound message and proposes it for approval. Run 2 (spawned after approval) executes the approved message by writing it to a context file.
body.how_it_works:
Run 1: draft message -> emit decision_required -> land PENDING_APPROVAL
Human: approve (optionally edit) or reject via /approvals
Run 2 (spawned): read approved_output -> record sent=true + sent_message

inputs.description: Set to "approved" by the approval system when spawning run 2.
inputs.label: Approval decision (set by system on run 2)
inputs.name: decision

inputs.description: The approved (possibly edited) output from run 1.
inputs.label: Approved output (set by system on run 2)
inputs.name: approved_output

body.long_description:
This worker proves the S47 HITL approval flow end-to-end.

Phase 1 (run 1): draft an outbound message for a given prospect and emit
decision_required so a human can review before anything is sent.

Phase 2 (run 2): reads inputs.decision and inputs.approved_output, then
executes the approved message and records the side-effect as the output
fields sent=true + sent_message.

Idempotency constraint: only run 2 fires the side-effect. Run 1 NEVER
sends anything.
body.name: Outbound approval demo
use_cases: Approve outbound recruiting emails before they reach candidates.
Gate any worker side-effect behind a human decision step.
Test the two-run HITL respawn flow in a safe, harmless way.

body.long_description:
Cron-driven v0 adapter that connects Slack to the Workeros workspace agent.

When triggered, it:
1. Fetches recent @floom mentions from the configured Slack channel.
2. For each unprocessed mention, calls POST /chat with the message text
   and an optional conversation_id (keyed by Slack thread_ts).
3. Streams the workspace agent reply and posts it back to the Slack thread.

Upgrade path: replace cron trigger with a Slack webhook/Composio event trigger
once the workspace exposes a webhook receiver.

use_cases: Embed the workspace agent in Slack so team members can query workers via DM or channel.
Route Slack @floom mentions to the workspace agent for ops triage.
Keep Slack thread follow-ups attached to the matching workspace conversation.

let the worker keep you updated automatically each week.
